text.p: UK property group Chelsfield Plc will continue to focus on large-scale retail projects, its chairman Elliott Bernerd said on Tuesday following the release of increased interim pre-tax profits.
"The market has a good feel at the moment. We should continue to major on large-scale retailing," Bernerd told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Earlier the group, which is working on a large retail and leisure development at White City in the west of London, announced pre-tax profits for the period of 6.0 million stg.
This compared with 4.3 million stg for the same period in the previous year. The group also announced an increased interim dividend of 1.2 pence per share, up from 1.1 pence.
Bernerd said the focus on retail developments reflected "the changing pattern of what is happening on the High Street".
He said the company was pleased with it progress and the performance of its Merry Hill shopping centre in the West Midlands and its other operations.
The group's development of the White City site was, Bernerd said, still under discussion with the local authority. But it would like to make a start by next summer, he added.
"There's a huge amount of work to be done," he said.

Bernerd declined to comment on who the likely tenants of the scheme would be, but he said the response had been "terrific", with "enormous interest" in the centre from tenants involved in both retailing and leisure.

He was unwilling to detail another London development at Paddington Basin, which has been linked with Chelsfield, beyond confirming that it had acquired Paddington Basin Ltd with a partner, from Trafalgar House.
"This is a substantial urban regeneration project and we are very enthusiastic about it," he said but added it was premature to talk about it in any detail.

Chelsfield's other projects include some on the River Thames and it had gained local authority approval for planning consent at its remaining riverside location, Camelford House, for a new residential development with 216 apartments.
Bernerd said the group liked the residential sector but its balance sheet would remain heavily weighted to retailing.
He said its U.S. operation was performing well and now accounted for around 10 percent of the balance sheet.
Chelsfield's recent rights issue, which raised 102 million stg net of expenses, had put the group in the position of being able to pursue the projects it wanted to, Bernerd said.
There were no immediate plans to raise further funds. "At the moment we consider we have enough cash resources to do what we want," he said.
